scenes.title: What is GIS Terrain Mapping?
scenes.narration: GIS terrain mapping creates digital 3D models of Earth's surface, transforming raw data into actionable insights. A single high-resolution terrain map can contain billions of data points, crucial for understanding landscapes.

scenes.title: Data Acquisition Methods
scenes.narration: Diverse sensors acquire terrain data, including satellite imagery, airborne LiDAR, and drone photogrammetry. LiDAR can measure elevation with centimeter-level accuracy by emitting pulsed lasers.

scenes.title: Digital Elevation Models (DEMs)
scenes.narration: The core output is a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), a grid of cells where each cell stores an elevation value. This structured data forms the foundation for all subsequent terrain analysis.

scenes.title: Urban Planning & Disaster Response
scenes.narration: In urban planning, GIS maps optimize infrastructure and visualize development. For disaster response, they model flood risk and identify evacuation routes, saving lives and resources with up to 90% accuracy.

scenes.title: Future of Spatial Intelligence
scenes.narration: GIS terrain mapping fuels advancements in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and smart cities. The global GIS market is projected to reach over $20 billion by 2027, enabling more intelligent and sustainable decisions.
